data.name: Bharini
data.gender_notes: Bharini is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A woman who carries the mountain on her head or shoulders. This name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Bharati', meaning 'bringer of joy'. It is also associated with the goddess Parvati, who carried the mountain Kailash on her head. The name Bharini carries the meaning “Mountain carrier” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bharini usually hope their child will grow to embody mountain carrier and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carrier of spiritual burdens and joys
data.etymology: Bharini belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mountain carrier.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bharini total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bharini has deep rooted cultural significance in Hindu history and mythology. It is a name that embodies strength, resilience, and a deep connection to tradition. It is a reminder of the strong and dedicated women in Hindu culture who perform the arduous task of carrying heavy loads on their heads. This name also has ties to the goddess Parvati, who is known for her devotion, strength, and compassion.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Bharini holds a deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. It is a reminder of the divine qualities of strength, dedication, and devotion. It is also a reminder of the importance of carrying the burdens of life with grace and dignity. The name is especially significant for those who seek to embody the qualities of Parvati, the goddess of love, beauty, and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bharini symbolizes the steadfast and devoted soul, rooted in the land of India (Bharat), forever nurturing and preserving its rich cultural heritage. Her name evokes a sense of strength, resilience, and unwavering commitment to the eternal spirit of India.
